content.name: Document Bootstrap
content.description: Generic coordination document contract for recording a bootstrap provider's response lifecycle. It defines only the provider-facing response operations and the state they materialize. Concrete documents decide how bootstrap is requested and which bootstrap input is supplied.

bootstrapProviderChannel.description: Participant channel for the bootstrap provider.

documentSession.description: Running document session made available after successful bootstrap.

error.description: Optional explanation recorded when bootstrap is declined or fails.

content.name: Document Bootstrap Completed
content.description: Response reporting that a bootstrap provider successfully started the requested logical document and made a running session of that document available to the requester or to the participant on whose behalf bootstrap was requested.

documentSession.description: Provider-neutral reference to the running session made available to the requester or to the participant on whose behalf bootstrap was requested. Its initialDocument identifies the requested logical document.

content.name: Document Bootstrap Declined
content.description: Response reporting that a bootstrap provider declined the requested bootstrap.

reason.description: Optional explanation for declining the request.

content.name: Document Bootstrap Failed
content.description: Response reporting that a bootstrap provider failed to complete started bootstrap work.

error.description: Explanation of why the started bootstrap work failed.

content.name: Document Bootstrap In Progress
content.description: Response reporting that a bootstrap provider started the requested bootstrap.

content.name: Document Bootstrap Requested
content.description: Request asking the participant addressed by recipientChannel to bootstrap the supplied initial document with any participant resolution input and optional initial Messages. The emitting document decides how and when to create the request.

requesterChannel.description: Optional channel key in the requesting document whose participant is asking for bootstrap.

participantMappings.description: Optional participant resolution input for target channels whose actors are not already defined by the target document.

initialMessages.description: Optional Messages supplied as bootstrap input for the target document.

content.name: Participant Mapping
content.description: Bootstrap input for one abstract channel in a target document. It identifies the participant whom the bootstrap provider should resolve or contact for that channel. The mapping intentionally contains only provider-neutral participant resolution hints.

channelName.description: Abstract channel key in the target document.

accountId.description: Optional account identifier understood by the bootstrap provider.

email.description: Optional email address used to resolve or invite the participant.

content.name: Crypto Ed25519 Verify
content.description: Verifies an Ed25519 signature over the exact UTF-8 bytes of message.

content.name: Currency
content.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., USD, EUR).

content.name: Document
content.description:
Broad base type for semantic documents that describe what they are directly.
Use the top-level `kind` field for business-level meaning on top of the
concrete document family type.

kind.description: Human-readable business meaning for this document.

content.name: Named Event
content.description:
Lightweight coordination event identified by the instance `name` field.
Use it to emit, forward, or match a well-known signal
without introducing a dedicated repository event type.

content.name: Payment
content.description:
Broad document family for a value-moving or value-committing document.
Use the top-level `kind` to describe the payment intent,
such as `Invoice Settlement`, `Payout`, or `Milestone Payment`.

content.name: Profile
content.description:
Broad document family for a public-facing identity or presence.
Use the top-level `kind` to describe the specific profile,
such as `Business Profile`, `Creator Profile`, or `Directory Listing`.

content.name: Record
content.description:
Broad document family for a single item that belongs somewhere.
Use the top-level `kind` to express the specific business meaning, such as
`Shopping Order`, `Comment`, `Invoice`, or `Report`.

content.name: Relationship
content.description:
Broad document family for a shared document between parties.
Use the top-level `kind` to describe the specific relationship shape,
such as `Service Agreement`, `Partnership Proposal`, or `Legal Engagement`.

content.name: Request
content.description:
Broad document family for a request for something from a provider or participant.
Use the top-level `kind` to describe the specific request,
such as `Legal Review Request`, `Service Request`, or `Intake Request`.

content.name: Response
content.description:
Broad document family for a response to a request.
Use the top-level `kind` to describe the specific response,
such as `Legal Review Response`, `Report Delivery`, or `Intake Response`.

content.name: Service
content.description:
Broad document family for a document that is itself a service offering.
Use the top-level `kind` to describe the specific offering,
such as `Legal Service`, `Tutoring Service`, or `Analytics Service`.

categories.description: Optional broad categories used to help humans discover the service.

content.name: Space
content.description:
Broad document family for a long-lived place in some reality.
Use it directly as the document `type` and express business meaning through
the top-level `kind`, such as `Online Shop`, `Legal Office`, or `Research Lab`.

website.description: Optional primary website or canonical public URL for this space.

content.name: Task
content.description:
Broad document family for a bounded unit of work over time.
Use the top-level `kind` to describe the business task,
such as `Weekly Report`, `Inbox Monitoring`, or `Order Triage`.

content.name: API Call
content.description:
Source specialization for a programmatic request submitted through an API credential, service integration, client
registration, signed request, webhook, or similar non-interactive interface. API Call identifies the submission
channel; it does not by itself say whether the actor was a principal, an agent, or another provider-defined actor.

API Call is useful because many documents distinguish low-risk automation from high-risk principal actions. A bank
transfer document might allow API calls to add notes or upload receipts, while requiring an interactive browser
session for final authorization. A procurement workflow might allow an agent to request quotes through an API but not
to commit funds. These decisions belong to Blue documents and processor policies, not to the Timeline Provider.

The provider's responsibility is to authenticate the API credential or client under its infrastructure rules,
confirm that the caller is allowed to append to the relevant timeline or submit the relevant event, and record the
source attribution accurately. The provider does not need to know what every Blue document will later do with the
message.

apiKeyId.description:
Opaque or provider-defined identifier of the API credential, client registration, integration, or signing key used to
submit the request. It should be stable enough for the provider and authorized auditors to trace, revoke, and review
the credential, but it need not reveal secret credential material.

content.name: Actor
content.description:
Base coordination type for verifiable actor attribution. An Actor describes the accountable entity on whose authority
a timeline entry, operation request, response, status change, customer action, or other coordination event was
produced. The actor may be a human principal, an organization, an automated service, an AI agent, a device, or a
provider-defined specialization, but the crucial semantic point is that the event source is making an attribution
claim that downstream documents can inspect.

Actor attribution is not permission by itself. It is evidence about who or what caused an action. A Timeline Provider
or other event source authenticates the party trying to append an entry to a timeline and records the actor category
and any provider-specific audit fields. Blue documents then decide, through Actor Policy, operation-specific rules,
or domain-specific logic, whether that actor is allowed to perform the requested operation. Processors MUST NOT infer
actor category from message text; they use the explicit actor node supplied with the event or timeline entry.

Concrete actor types should precisely state what the provider is asserting. Principal Actor means the action is
attributed directly to the principal or account owner. Agent Actor means the action is attributed to delegated
automation acting on behalf of a principal. Provider-specific actor types may describe UI authentication strength,
API credentials, agent sessions, delegation references, device identity, assurance level, or other auditable
evidence. Because the description of an actor type is identity-bearing Blue content, it should be written as the
normative semantic contract of that actor type, not as informal documentation.

content.name: Actor Policy
content.description:
Processor-visible policy marker that constrains which actor and source categories may invoke named operations. Actor
Policy turns actor/source attribution into enforceable workflow rules. It lets a document require direct principal
action for sensitive operations such as authorization, capture, cancellation, consent, or contract amendment, while
permitting delegated agents or API calls for lower-risk operations such as adding notes, requesting information, or
preparing drafts.

The policy is keyed by operation name. Each operation entry can constrain the actor category with `requiresActor`,
require a source category with `requiresSource`, and/or reject a source category with `excludeSource`. The core
actor categories are `principal`, `agent`, and `any`. The core source categories are `browserSession`, `apiCall`, and
`documentRequest`. These are intentionally broad categories. Domain-specific policies may refine them by requiring
a specialized actor or source type in the operation runtime, such as a strongly authenticated browser session or a
provider-specific agent delegation.

Actor Policy is a marker. It does not handle events, issue patches, or inspect timelines by itself. A supported
operation channel/runtime reads it when evaluating an Operation Request or comparable event. If the event's actor or
source does not satisfy the operation's policy, the operation is rejected or the scope terminates according to the
hosting processor's rules. Timeline Providers are not responsible for enforcing this document policy; they provide
infrastructure, attribution, append authorization, ordering, storage, and completeness guarantees. Blue documents use
Actor Policy to decide how to interpret those attributed entries.

operations.description:
Per-operation constraints keyed by operation name. Each operation value may specify actor/source requirements.
Missing fields mean this policy marker does not constrain that dimension for the operation.

requiresActor.description:
Required actor category for the operation. `principal` means the actor must be a Principal Actor or compatible
subtype. `agent` means the actor must be an Agent Actor or compatible subtype. `any` means the operation does
not restrict the actor category at this policy level, though the operation runtime may still apply stricter
rules.

requiresSource.description:
Required source category for the operation. `browserSession` requires an interactive UI/source session,
`apiCall` requires a programmatic API source, and `documentRequest` requires a request originating from another
Blue document or document session. Omit this field when the policy does not require a particular source.

excludeSource.description:
Disallowed source category for the operation. This can prohibit a category even when the actor is otherwise
acceptable. For example, an operation may allow any actor but exclude `apiCall` to require a non-API source.

content.name: Agent Actor
content.description:
Actor specialization for a non-human, automated, delegated, or AI-assisted actor. An Agent Actor means the event
source attributes the action to automation operating on behalf of another actor rather than to the principal acting
directly. This distinction is fundamental for safe automation: routine operations may be delegated to agents, while
sensitive operations may require direct principal action.

A Timeline Provider or event source is not expected to understand every Blue document that may later consume the
entry, and it is not responsible for deciding whether the message is valid for a particular document. Its role is to
authenticate and authorize the party that appends to the timeline under the provider's own rules, record the actor
attribution it can verify, preserve the entry, assign ordering information, and provide completeness/finality
guarantees. A provider may verify that an agent has permission to append to a timeline or act for an account under a
delegated credential, but Blue documents independently enforce their own Actor Policy and operation rules.

The `onBehalfOf` field identifies the principal or actor whose authority is being used. Concrete agent types should
add fields that make the delegation auditable: agent identity, session reference, delegation document, allowed scope,
issuing provider, revocation context, or model/runtime details where appropriate. The goal is not to pretend that the
agent is a human; the goal is to make automation explicit, attributable, auditable, and policy-checkable.

onBehalfOf.description:
Actor on whose behalf this agent is acting. This should normally be a Principal Actor or provider-specific principal
reference. It is an attribution field, not a standalone authorization grant. A document should still check its own
policies before accepting the requested operation.

content.name: All Timelines Channel
content.description:
Dynamic union channel that matches entries from all Timeline-derived channels in the same contracts scope. It is the
compact form for operations that should be callable by every current participant, such as chat or purpose/role
confirmation. When participant channels are added or removed through normal document updates, this channel follows the
current document structure automatically.

The union has no timeline or actor of its own. It delegates eligibility to the same-scope Timeline Channels, each of
which supplies its own timeline and actor binding. If several child channels accept the same entry, this channel
produces one logical delivery to handlers bound to the All Timelines Channel key. Its checkpoint is independent from
checkpoints of child channels used directly elsewhere in the document.

All Timelines Channel does not create a new timeline, does not merge provider proofs, and does not change ordering.
The feeder/runtime must still obtain completeness for every timeline that participates in the current document scope
and must deliver entries in the canonical deterministic order. The channel only simplifies authoring by avoiding a
manually maintained Composite Timeline Channel for "everyone at the table".

content.name: Authority
content.description: Base type for evidence explaining why an actor may act for another actor or exercise authority not available through its direct channel attribution.

content.name: Browser Session
content.description:
Source specialization for an authenticated interactive browser, mobile, or user-interface session. Browser Session
records that the event source observed the request through an interactive session rather than a background API
credential. It is often combined with Principal Actor when a document wants evidence of direct human involvement.

Browser Session does not, by itself, guarantee a particular authentication strength. A concrete subtype may define
password login, two-factor authentication, biometric verification, hardware key challenge, regulated strong customer
authentication, or other assurance details. Documents that require those stronger conditions should check the
concrete subtype or additional fields, not merely the base Browser Session type.

A Timeline Provider or event source authenticates the session and records the source. Blue documents later use that
source attribution to decide whether a requested operation meets their policy. The provider is infrastructure: it
validates the session and appends the entry; it does not need to understand the business meaning of the message.

uiSessionNonce.description:
Provider-generated identifier for the UI session or interaction context. It may be opaque outside the provider, but
it should be sufficient for provider-side audit, incident review, revocation, and correlation with authentication
records. It MUST NOT contain secret session credentials.

content.name: Chat Message
content.description:
Free-text Message for humans. Chat Message records text intended for
participants or auditors when no structured, machine-actionable Message type
is required.

As a Coordination/Message it supports requestId, inResponseTo, threadId, and
recipientChannel. recipientChannel directs attention but does not make the
Message private. A Chat Message may comment on a Request but never fulfils it;
only a Coordination/Response answers a Request, and only concrete operation
contracts perform actions.

message.description:
Textual content of the Message. Exact spelling, whitespace, and Unicode code
points are part of the Blue value.

content.name: Chat Workflow Operation
content.description:
Standard operation for chat at a document table. A document that wants all participants to chat can define an
All Timelines Channel and one Chat Workflow Operation on that channel. The workflow emits the Chat Message request
payload as a normal coordination event so it appears in document event projections and audit views.

Sequential Workflow Operation defines steps as append-only. Chat Workflow Operation seeds that list with a standard
first step that emits the chat event that arrived in the operation request; document-specific chat behavior can append
validation, moderation, indexing, notification, or projection steps after that standard emission step without changing
the inherited prefix.

This type is intentionally simple: chat is not authority, payment truth, permission truth, or workflow approval. Use
domain-specific operations and strong response types for machine-actionable commitments.

steps.description:
Workflow steps for chat processing. The first inherited step emits the arriving Chat Message request payload as a
coordination event.

items.name: Emit Arrived Chat Event
items.description: Emits the Chat Message payload from the arriving Operation Request.

content.name: Composite Timeline Channel
content.description:
Channel contract that groups several same-scope Timeline Channels into one union channel. A Composite Timeline
Channel matches when any referenced child channel would accept the delivered event. It is useful when a workflow
should react to a family of participant timelines while binding handlers to one logical channel key.

The composite has no timeline or actor of its own. Each referenced Timeline Channel supplies its own timeline and actor
binding, and the composite delegates event eligibility to those children. If several children accept the same entry,
the composite produces one logical delivery to handlers bound to the composite key. The composite's checkpoint is
independent from checkpoints of child channels used directly elsewhere in the document.

This type does not create global consensus and does not collapse the child timelines into one storage log. Each child
timeline retains its provider, completeness, actor attribution, and trust model. The composite only simplifies routing
inside the document. A correct feeder/processor must still preserve deterministic ordering across the relevant
timelines using provider completeness guarantees and the Blue Contracts checkpoint model.

channels.description:
Same-scope contract-map keys of Timeline Channel contracts included in this composite. The list order is not a
cross-timeline ordering rule; event ordering must be established by the feeder/provider layer and deterministic
processor sorting.

content.name: Compute
content.description:
Workflow step that evaluates Blue Expression Objects (BEX): deterministic programs written as Blue data. Compute is
for logic that should live inside the document instead of host code. A Compute step can read a Blue document view,
host-provided bindings, constants, variables, prior workflow results, the triggering event, and the current contract;
then it can compute structured Blue-compatible data such as booleans, numbers, strings, objects, lists, patch
changesets, event payloads, validation results, and policy decisions.

BEX is not JavaScript, WASM, a network runtime, an LLM extension point, or a contract processor. It has no ambient
time, randomness, filesystem, network, database, asynchronous execution, or hidden mutable state in the core language.
Host capabilities are available only through explicitly registered `$intrinsic` processors identified by BlueId. A
BEX program does not mutate the document or perform external actions. It computes a deterministic result; the host
decides how to use that result, and document mutation still requires Update Document or processor patch semantics.

A BEX program is a Blue object tree. An object with exactly one key beginning with `$` is an operator. Objects with
ordinary keys are literal Blue-compatible objects whose children are evaluated recursively. Lists and scalar values
are literals unless nested inside an operator body. Because BEX programs are Blue data, they participate in the same
content identity and BlueId model as the documents that carry them.

BEX supports data access operators (`$document`, `$binding`, `$event`, `$steps`, `$currentContract`, `$var`, `$const`,
`$get`), type helpers (`$unwrap`, `$is`, `$kind`, `$isKind`, `$text`, `$integer`, `$number`, `$boolean`, `$object`,
`$list`), string and pointer operators (`$concat`, `$join`, `$split`, `$startsWith`, `$sliceAfter`, `$pointerJoin`),
logic and comparison (`$eq`, `$ne`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$and`, `$or`, `$not`, `$truthy`, `$empty`,
`$isEmpty`, `$exists`, `$coalesce`, `$default`), numeric operators (`$add`, `$subtract`, `$multiply`, `$divide`),
object/list operators (`$keys`, `$entries`, `$size`, `$listGet`, `$listConcat`, `$merge`, `$objectSet`,
`$pointerGet`, `$pointerSet`, `$map`, `$filter`, `$flatMap`, `$reduce`, `$some`, `$find`, `$findEntry`, `$includes`,
`$hasKey`, `$objectFromEntries`), conditionals (`$choose`), functions (`$call`), host extensions (`$intrinsic`),
literal/null/empty constructors (`$literal`, `$null`, `$emptyObject`, `$emptyList`), result helpers (`$changeset`,
`$events`, `$resultValue`), and deterministic failure/early-return helpers (`$returnIf`, `$fail`, `$failIf`).

BEX statements include `$let`, `$set`, `$if`, `$forEach`, `$appendChange`, `$appendChanges`, `$appendEvent`,
`$appendEvents`, `$call`, `$return`, `$returnIf`, `$fail`, and `$failIf`. `$let` may bind one variable or a `vars`
block. Without `order`, multi-bind variables are parallel and read the old frame. With `order`, bindings are
sequential and later bindings may read earlier ones. `$forEach` iterates lists in item order and objects in sorted key
order; it may bind item, key, and index variables.

`$document` reads the canonical document view by default and may explicitly read the resolved view when the host
exposes one. In a Blue Contracts workflow, BEX should read from the frozen processing snapshot or frozen working
document. If a prior Update Document step has previewed patches in the same sequential workflow, later Compute steps
should observe those previewed changes through the working document while the actual processor commit remains
buffered. This preserves read-your-writes behavior without materializing the whole document.

BEX function arguments can declare Blue patterns. Patterns are static Blue data, not BEX expressions. Runtime values
are checked with Blue's node/type matcher. BEX does not have a separate nominal type enum; it uses Blue patterns,
BlueIds, and Blue language matching. Name containers such as `functions`, `constants`, `args`, and `$call.args` must
not use Blue reserved keys or invalid reserved names as user-defined identifiers.

Evaluation is deterministic and gas-metered. BEX gas charges expression/value construction work: compilation,
operator evaluation, reads, conversions, loops, collection operations, patch construction, event construction,
intrinsic calls, and output conversion. Blue Contracts separately charges actual patch application, Document Update
cascades, emitted-event routing, checkpoints, lifecycle, termination, and processor state changes. BEX gas therefore
accounts for computing result data, not for committing that data to the document.

expr.description:
Optional single BEX expression. When present without `do`, the expression result is the step result. Use this for
simple projections, predicates, one-value calculations, and compact policy checks.

do.description:
Ordered BEX statement body. Statements execute sequentially, may define variables, branch, iterate bounded
collections, append changes/events to result accumulators, call functions, return early, or fail deterministically.
They do not directly mutate the selected document.

definition.description:
Optional reference to a reusable Compute Definition containing functions and constants. A concrete workflow runtime
defines whether this is a contract-map key, BlueId reference, or another deterministic lookup. The lookup must be
stable for content identity and deterministic execution.

entry.description:
Entry function name to invoke when a definition or local functions are used. If omitted, the runtime uses the step's
inline `expr` or `do` body according to Compute semantics.

constants.description:
Literal constants available through `$const`. Unknown constants fail at compile time. Constant names are user-defined
identifiers and must not collide with Blue reserved keys or invalid names.

functions.description:
Local BEX function definitions keyed by function name. Functions may declare required arguments using static Blue
patterns and may contain `expr` or `do` bodies. Unknown functions, missing arguments, and extra arguments fail
deterministically.

emitEvents.description:
When true, a result object containing an `events` list requests those events to be emitted by the workflow/processor.
Compute itself still does not route events; the processor validates, charges, enqueues, bridges, and exposes them.

returnResult.description:
When true, the computed result is stored under the step name for later workflow steps. When false, the step may still
contribute events or changes according to the host workflow semantics but does not export a step result.

gasLimit.description:
Optional maximum BEX gas for this step. If omitted, the host or workflow runtime chooses the applicable default. Gas
exhaustion causes deterministic compute failure.

content.name: Compute Definition
content.description:
Reusable BEX definition containing constants and functions that can be referenced by Compute steps. A Compute
Definition lets a document keep shared deterministic logic in one place while still representing that logic as Blue
data that affects document identity.

Constants are literal values accessed with `$const`. Functions are named BEX programs with optional static Blue
argument patterns. Definitions do not execute by themselves; a Compute step selects an entry function or imports the
definition's functions/constants into its compilation context.

Because this node is part of identity, changing a function body, argument pattern, constant, or description changes
the definition's BlueId and therefore changes the semantic identity of documents that reference it.

constants.description:
Literal named constants available to functions or referencing Compute steps through `$const`. Constant names are
static identifiers and must not use reserved Blue language keys.

functions.description:
Named BEX functions. Each function may declare argument patterns and either an `expr` or `do` body. Functions are
deterministic and have no ambient side effects.

content.name: Customer Action Requested
content.description:
Event requesting that a customer, user, or participant take an explicit action. This is typically emitted when an
automated workflow reaches a point that needs human review, consent, selection, confirmation, or additional input.

The event should describe the requested action in human-readable form and provide a deterministic list of allowed
actions. The response should be represented by Customer Action Responded or a domain-specific response event.

title.description: Title shown to the user or participant for the pending action.

message.description: Detailed human-readable explanation of what is being requested and why.

actions.description: Allowed action labels or structured options. Their order is the display/order preference.

label.description: User-facing action label shown in the pending action card.

variant.description: Optional button style variant. Supported values: primary | secondary | reject.

inputSchema.description: Optional input schema. If present, the selected action may collect user input.

inputRequired.description: Optional flag indicating whether input is required for this action.

inputTitle.description: Optional title displayed above the action input control.

inputPlaceholder.description: Optional placeholder/help text shown in the action input control.

content.name: Customer Action Responded
content.description:
Event recording a customer's response to a previously requested action. It captures which action label was selected,
optional input supplied by the customer, and the response time when available.

This event is not proof of authorization by itself. Actor and source attribution should come from the enclosing
Timeline Entry or event source. Workflows should check Actor Policy when the response authorizes sensitive behavior.

actionLabel.description: Label of the selected action from the corresponding Customer Action Requested event.

input.description: Optional structured input supplied by the customer. Shape depends on the requested action.

respondedAt.description: Optional response timestamp in the provider/application time model.

content.name: Customer Consent Revoked
content.description:
Event indicating that a customer or participant revoked a previously granted consent, authorization, or permission.
Workflows should treat this as a high-priority signal and re-check any operation that depends on the revoked consent.

The event records an optional reason and timestamp. Actor/source attribution should be supplied by the enclosing
Timeline Entry or event source so that processors can determine whether the revocation came from an authorized
principal or an allowed delegate.

reason.description: Optional human-readable or structured reason for revocation.

revokedAt.description: Timestamp when revocation was recorded by the source or provider.

content.name: Document Anchor
content.description:
Passive declaration of a stable named incoming connection point. The
enclosing Document Anchors dictionary key is the actual anchor name. This
value carries only optional authoring guidance; it does not grant access,
validate an incoming link, execute behavior, or require eager indexing.

template.description:
Optional Blue document template recommendation for documents linking to
this anchor. It is authoring and bootstrap guidance only, not validation,
automatic execution, or a condition for retaining an incoming link.

content.name: Document Anchors
content.description:
Passive dictionary of named incoming connection points that other documents
may target. Each dictionary key is the exact anchor name; values provide
optional guidance. Anchors are part of a document's public link interface
when authored in effective root contracts.

content.name: Document Bootstrap Completed
content.description:
Lifecycle/coordination event indicating that a requested document bootstrap completed successfully. It records the
resulting document identifier so the requester can continue interacting with the new document or session.

documentId.description: Identifier, reference, or BlueId of the bootstrapped document/session, according to the bootstrap runtime.

content.name: Document Bootstrap Failed
content.description:
Lifecycle/coordination event indicating that a document bootstrap request failed. The `reason` field should explain
the deterministic failure cause or provider-specific rejection reason.

content.name: Document Bootstrap Responded
content.description:
Response event for a document bootstrap request. It records the resulting status and optional reason. Concrete
systems may use the more specific Completed or Failed events when they want clearer type-level distinction.

status.description: Bootstrap response status. Prefer a Document Status specialization where possible.

reason.description: Optional reason explaining success, failure, or pending state.

content.name: Document Link
content.description:
Passive declaration of one outgoing connection to a specific Blue document.
The target is identified by the Content BlueId of its initial document state.
A missing anchor targets the document root; a present anchor names one exact
incoming connection point declared by the target.

initialDocument.description:
Target document in its initial state. Authors may materialize the initial
document or use an equivalent pure Blue reference containing its blueId.
The referenced identity, not any later document state or session, is the
target document identifier.

anchor.description:
Optional exact Document Anchors dictionary key. When absent, this link
targets the document root. The value is opaque author-authored Text:
spelling, whitespace, case, and Unicode normalization are significant.

content.name: Document Links
content.description:
Passive dictionary of named outgoing document-link declarations. Dictionary
keys organize authoring and may communicate local purpose, but do not form
link identity. Every value is a Coordination/Document Link. Equivalent
values under different keys describe the same effective endpoint.

content.name: Document Request
content.description:
Source specialization for a request that originated from another Blue document or document-processing session. It is
used when one document asks another document to perform an operation, provide data, bootstrap state, or respond to a
pending action.

Document Request is a source category, not an actor category. The actor may be a principal or agent; the source says
the action was mediated through another document. This is useful for policies that allow document-to-document
automation for some operations while requiring browser-session principal confirmation for others.

documentId.description: Identifier or reference of the source document or document session that produced the request.

epoch.description:
Optional monotonically increasing version, epoch, or processing counter for the source document. It helps recipients
detect stale requests and reason about document evolution.

content.name: Document Status
content.description:
Base type for document status markers. A Document Status summarizes the current lifecycle or business state of a
coordination document in a compact, machine-readable form.

Concrete statuses specialize this type by fixing the `mode` field and may use
their concrete type to distinguish business outcomes that share a lifecycle
mode. Status values are Blue content: changing status changes document
identity and may trigger Document Update channels or workflows.

mode.description:
Canonical lifecycle mode. Concrete status types fix this value to `pending`,
`active`, or `terminated`; the concrete type distinguishes outcomes such as
completion, failure, and decline.

content.name: Event
content.description:
Base coordination type for Blue event payloads. An Event is a Blue node that may be placed in a Timeline Entry,
emitted by a workflow, routed through a channel, or recorded for audit. Event itself defines no operation semantics;
concrete event types such as Operation Request, Chat Message, Status Change, Customer Action Requested, or domain
events provide the fields that processors and handlers understand.

Events are passive content. A Blue Contracts processor treats delivered event nodes as read-only. Matching,
adaptation, authorization, and side effects are defined by channels, handlers, workflows, and policies. Because event
nodes are Blue content, their exact fields, values, names, and descriptions participate in identity when they are
hashed or stored.

content.name: Inform User About Pending Action
content.description:
Workflow/operation type that asks the system to notify a user about a pending action. It is typically used when a
document needs human attention: approval, consent, data entry, signature, correction, or review.

This type describes the notification request, not proof that the user has responded. A response should be represented
by Customer Action Responded or another explicit event. The `expectedRequest` field can help the UI or notification
system explain what kind of response should be sent back.

operation.description: Operation name associated with the pending action.

channel.description: Channel or delivery route to use for informing the user.

expectedRequest.description: Shape or description of the response expected from the user.

content.name: Lifecycle Event
content.description:
Base event type for processor lifecycle notifications. Lifecycle events describe processor-state transitions such as
initialization, termination, bootstrap completion, or failure. They are distinct from domain events such as chat
messages or operation requests.

Lifecycle events are emitted by processor or workflow infrastructure to make state transitions observable and
auditable. A Blue document may listen for them through Lifecycle Event Channels or domain-specific coordination
workflows, but the event itself remains passive Blue content.

content.name: Message
content.description: Base type for addressed, threadable communication between participants and documents. A Message may target a recipient channel, belong to a thread, and answer another Message. Requests, Responses, chat messages, operation requests, lifecycle messages, and document-emitted asks are all Messages, so one correlation model covers questions and answers, offers and counter-offers, asks and fulfilment, and free-form chat.

requestId.description: Optional application-level correlation key. It may group retries, provider work, or multiple messages associated with one logical request. It is not a substitute for inResponseTo, which identifies an exact Message occurrence.

threadId.description: Optional thread key grouping related Messages without requiring a consumer to walk an inResponseTo chain.

recipientChannel.description: Optional channel key identifying the participant this Message is addressed to. When absent, the Message is addressed to the table as a whole or to the document itself. Addressing does not make a Message private; visibility follows the enclosing document and timeline rules.

inResponseTo.description: Optional reference to the Message being answered, normally a pure { blueId: ... } reference to the exact Message occurrence or an equivalent materialized node. Any Message may answer any Message. Chains form a conversation tree; threadId provides direct grouping.

content.name: Operation
content.description:
Base handler contract type describing a named operation supported by a document or scope. An Operation gives a stable
name to a business action, binds that action to a same-scope effective handler channel, and describes the expected
request payload shape.

Operation is the common interface for operation handlers. A plain Operation declares the channel and request shape;
concrete operation types such as Sequential Workflow Operation provide the executable behavior. Actor Policy and
source policy typically refer to operation names when deciding whether a Timeline Entry or Operation Request may be
processed.

request.description:
Expected request payload shape or description for this operation. Concrete operation runtimes may use this for event
matching, validation, or documentation.

channel.description:
Same-scope effective channel key used to discover and invoke this Operation handler. An Operation Request may be
accepted through a different eligible source channel; the feeder validates source and authority constraints, and a
supporting processor routes the accepted request to this effective channel without transferring source-channel
checkpoint ownership.

content.name: Operation Request
content.description: Request to invoke one named operation through one effective channel. The enclosing Timeline Entry supplies actor attribution and any mandate-backed authority. A feeder verifies source-channel eligibility, mandate authority, and document-version constraints before passing the entry to a processor.

operation.description: Required operation contract key/name to invoke.

document.description: Optional current target document state on which the invocation is based. The value may be materialized or represented by an equivalent pure BlueId reference.

requireExactDocumentVersion.description: When true, the feeder passes the request only if document equals the current target state. When false or absent, a newer state may be accepted according to the feeder's document-version eligibility policy.

content.name: Participant Purpose
content.description: Participant-visible declaration of why an actor is present in a document and which activities it intends to perform. Purpose is explanatory state, not authority, and must never replace mandate verification.

statements.description: Ordered purpose statements declared by the participant.

content.name: Principal Actor
content.description:
Actor specialization for an action attributed directly to a principal: a person, organization, account owner, or
other primary authority recognized by the event source. A Principal Actor means the provider is asserting that the
action was performed under the principal's own authority, not by a delegated agent acting independently on the
principal's behalf.

This type does not specify how the provider authenticated the principal. A concrete subtype can describe a browser
session, biometric challenge, API credential treated as direct principal control, hardware key, bank login, or
government identity proof. The important invariant is semantic attribution: when a Blue document asks whether an
operation was performed by a principal, a Principal Actor or compatible subtype is the category it is checking.

Principal Actor also does not automatically authorize every operation. A document may still require a particular
source, stronger authentication, a specific account, a particular organization role, or additional domain-specific
conditions. This type supplies the actor category used by those policies.

content.name: Purpose Statement
content.description: One participant-visible purpose statement. It may describe an authorized representative role, an intended request pattern and response operation, or a simple non-provider role such as observing. Purpose does not grant authority.

onBehalfOf.description: Optional authority explaining whom the participant represents. A mandate-backed purpose uses Mandate/Mandate Authority, which includes the represented actor and mandate.

event.description: Optional request event type or pattern the participant intends to handle.

respondsWith.description: Optional operation selectors the participant may use in response.

summary.description: Optional human-readable explanation of the participant's purpose.

content.name: Request
content.description: A Message that solicits an answer. It establishes the expectation that the participant addressed by recipientChannel, or a suitable participant at the table when recipientChannel is absent, may eventually send a Response whose inResponseTo points to this Request. A Request may itself answer another Message, such as a counter-offer or clarifying question. Concrete request types define their payload and domain-specific recipient semantics.

content.name: Response
content.description: A Message that answers a Request. A single Request may receive multiple Responses, including responses from several participants or successive responses from one participant. A Response does not by itself perform an operation unless its concrete type and enclosing document contracts define that behavior.

inResponseTo.description: Required reference to the exact Coordination/Request occurrence answered by this Response.

content.name: Sequential Workflow
content.description:
Handler contract that executes an ordered list of workflow steps after its bound channel delivers an event. Sequential
Workflow is the standard coordination runtime for expressing document-owned logic without embedding host code. It
reads the channelized payload, runs each step in order, records step results under step names when applicable, and
returns processor effects such as patches, triggered events, explicit gas, or termination requests.

The workflow is sequential: later steps can read earlier step results through `$steps` and can observe prior Update
Document steps through the workflow's working document. The working document should be frozen/snapshot-backed and
advanced by the same patch, conformance, dynamic generalization, and Type Generalization Policy rules that the Blue
Contracts processor will use at commit time. This gives read-your-writes behavior without materializing the entire
document as mutable state.

Sequential Workflow does not weaken the Blue Contracts processor model. Patches are still applied through Update
Document. Events are still emitted through Trigger Event or result emission. Boundary rules, reserved-key protection,
post-patch type soundness, generalization, Document Update cascades, checkpoints, and gas accounting remain processor
responsibilities. The workflow only provides a deterministic authoring/runtime structure for arranging these steps.

steps.description:
Ordered list of workflow steps. The list order is execution order. A step may expose a named result for later steps,
but actual document mutation and event routing still occur through processor-defined effect application.

content.name: Sequential Workflow Operation
content.description:
Concrete Operation handler whose implementation is an ordered Sequential Workflow. Because Operation extends Handler,
a Sequential Workflow Operation is discovered and invoked as a same-scope handler bound to its channel.

A Sequential Workflow Operation is still invoked like any other Operation: callers post an Operation Request naming
the operation contract key and its effective channel, and the request payload must conform to this operation's request
shape. The request may be accepted through a different eligible source channel. A supporting processor routes it to
the operation's effective channel while preserving source-channel checkpoint semantics. The workflow then runs the
declared steps deterministically and returns effects such as triggered events or document updates through the Blue
Contracts processor.

Use this for document-owned behavior where the operation interface and implementation should live together in a single
contract entry. A plain Operation can still declare the operation interface when a runtime or document chooses to bind
the implementation separately.

steps.description:
Append-only ordered workflow steps to run when this operation is invoked. The steps have the same semantics as steps
in a Sequential Workflow: Compute steps compute data, Update Document steps request processor-managed patches, and
Trigger Event steps emit Blue events. The processor remains responsible for validation, patch application, event
routing, deterministic ordering, gas, and post-patch type soundness.

The append-only merge policy preserves inherited workflow prefixes. Subtypes and concrete documents may append
additional steps, but must not replace, reorder, or positionally overlay inherited steps.

content.name: Sequential Workflow Step
content.description:
Base type for one ordered step inside a Sequential Workflow. A step describes deterministic work to perform after a
workflow operation or channel delivery matches. Concrete step types include Compute, Update Document, Trigger Event,
JavaScript Code in legacy runtimes, or other supported deterministic steps.

A step may read the event, current contract, prior step results, and the workflow's current working document view. It
must not bypass the processor's mutation rules. Steps that compute data return step results. Steps that request
mutation do so through Update Document and the Blue Contracts patch/generalization pipeline. Steps that emit events
do so through Trigger Event or result emission semantics.

content.name: Source
content.description:
Base coordination type for source attribution: how an event, request, or timeline entry reached the event source.
Actor answers "who or what caused this action"; Source answers "through what channel or context was the action
submitted". The two dimensions are intentionally separate. A principal may act through a browser session or an API
call; an agent may also act through an API call or a provider-managed automation channel.

Source nodes are passive provenance content. They do not execute logic and do not authorize anything by themselves.
They let documents distinguish interactive UI sessions, API calls, document-to-document requests, blockchain
transactions, customer consent flows, or other submission contexts. Actor Policy and domain-specific operation rules
can then require or exclude source categories. For example, a document can require principal actor attribution and a
browser-session source for authorizing funds, while allowing API-call sources for low-risk status queries.

Concrete Source subtypes should state exactly what the provider observed and what an auditor can rely on. A source
type should not overclaim: if it only identifies an API credential, it should not imply interactive human presence;
if it only identifies a browser session, it should not imply a specific authentication strength unless the subtype
says so.

content.name: Status
content.description: Base coordination status marker. Concrete status types describe the current lifecycle or business state of a coordination document.

content.name: Status Change
content.description:
Event announcing that a status value has changed or should be observed as changed. Status Change is useful when a
workflow wants to notify participants or parent scopes about state progress without exposing an entire document
snapshot.

The `status` field carries the new status object. Consumers should use the status type and `mode` value rather than
parsing human-readable text.

status.description:
New status value. Usually a Document Status specialization such as Status Pending, Status In Progress, Status
Completed, or Status Failed.

content.name: Status Completed
content.description: Concrete Document Status meaning the relevant workflow, document bootstrap, customer action, or operation completed successfully. The fixed mode is `terminated`; the concrete type distinguishes successful completion.

content.name: Status Declined
content.description: Concrete Status Failed specialization for requested work that was declined before it started. It is terminal, produces no successful result, and remains compatible with consumers matching Status Failed.

content.name: Status Failed
content.description: Concrete Document Status meaning the relevant workflow, document bootstrap, customer action, or operation failed or was rejected. The fixed mode is `terminated`; the concrete type distinguishes failure.

content.name: Status In Progress
content.description: Concrete Document Status meaning work has started and is actively being processed, but no terminal success or failure has been reached. The fixed mode is `active`.

content.name: Status Pending
content.description: Concrete Document Status meaning work has not yet started, is waiting for external input, or is queued for later processing. The fixed mode is `pending`.

content.name: Terminate Processing
content.description:
Workflow step that requests graceful termination of the current processing scope. The request is buffered as the same
processor effect used by a Compute result containing `termination`. Previously buffered document changes and emitted
events are applied before termination according to Blue Contracts effect ordering, and later steps in the Sequential
Workflow are not evaluated.

The Blue Contracts processor owns the resulting Processing Terminated Marker, Document Processing Terminated lifecycle
event, scope deactivation, queue cutoff, and root or embedded-scope completion behavior. This step cannot request fatal
termination or target another scope.

reason.description:
Optional reason passed unchanged to graceful termination. Missing or empty Text produces no reason field in the
processor marker or lifecycle event.

content.name: Timeline
content.description:
A Timeline is an append-only, tamper-evident personal or institutional event log. It records entries associated with
one timeline identity, account, actor, service, organization, document, or provider-defined context. It can be used
as private storage, shared selectively with other parties, made public, or connected to Blue documents through
Timeline Channels. Blue document processing is one use case of timelines, not the definition of a timeline.

A Timeline Provider supplies infrastructure for timelines. Its core responsibilities are to authenticate and
authorize parties that append entries to a timeline, assign a timestamp to each accepted entry and, after the first,
make it strictly greater than the timestamp of the preceding accepted entry in that timeline, link entries to previous
entries where the timeline design requires a hash chain, expose entries to authorized readers, and issue
completeness/finality guarantees. A provider generally does not understand the business meaning of every message.
Someone may place arbitrary Blue messages on a timeline if the provider allows that party to append to that timeline.
Documents that later consume those entries decide whether the messages are relevant, valid, authorized, or
policy-compliant.

Completeness is the guarantee that makes deterministic multi-party processing possible. When a provider says there
are no entries with timestamp less than T, it is also promising that future entries it accepts will not be assigned a
timestamp less than T. Timestamps are unique and establish total order within one timeline. Equal timestamp values may
occur in different timelines and are ordered by deterministic feeder-profile tie-breakers. A blockchain-backed
provider can provide completeness only for finalized history and must define the finality rule. Completeness is about
a cross-timeline processing window and the absence of earlier entries; it is not a claim that message content is
semantically valid for a particular Blue document.

Timeline entries are normally hash-linked through `prevEntry`, making tampering detectable. Timestamp establishes
order within one timeline and supports cross-timeline ordering and completeness windows; actor and source establish
attribution; message contains the Blue payload. A Blue processor may use entries from several timelines, but it should
do so only after the relevant providers or finalized stores establish a complete processing window. This lets
independent processors merge individual perspectives deterministically without global consensus.

timelineId.description:
Stable provider- or application-defined identifier for this timeline. The identifier is used by channels, providers,
auditors, and participants to locate the append-only log. It should not be reused for a different history or owner
because readers treat all entries under the same identifier as one timeline perspective.

content.name: Timeline Channel
content.description: External Coordination channel backed by one timeline and bound to one actor in the containing document. A feeder uses both bindings to determine whether a Timeline Entry is eligible through this channel. The same timeline may be bound to several channels, but one input entry must never produce duplicate logical delivery solely because several bindings match.

timeline.description: Timeline whose entries may be accepted through this channel.

actor.description: Actor represented by this channel. A feeder matches this actor against the actor attributed on a candidate Timeline Entry.

content.name: Timeline Entry
content.description: Immutable entry in an append-only Timeline. The Timeline Provider assigns a timestamp that is unique and strictly increasing within the timeline, links the entry to its predecessor, and authenticates actor and available source attribution. A feeder validates, orders, and filters entries before passing eligible events to a processor.

prevEntry.description: Generic reference to the previous entry in the same timeline. Non-first entries should normally use a pure BlueId reference. The field is intentionally untyped so standard document processing can retain it as opaque audit evidence without materializing or validating the referenced history. The Timeline Provider or verifier validates it against the immediately preceding accepted entry. The first entry may omit this field.

timestamp.description: Microsecond timestamp assigned by the Timeline Provider. It is unique and strictly increasing within this timeline and is the authoritative intra-timeline ordering value. It also supports cross-timeline ordering and completeness windows under the provider profile.

actor.description: Actor attributed as the writer or submitter of this entry.

source.description: Optional provider-authenticated attribution of how the entry was submitted, such as through a browser session, API call, or document request. Source complements actor attribution and does not grant authority by itself. A policy that requires or excludes a source category must treat an absent source as not satisfying that source constraint.

onBehalfOf.description: Optional authority under which actor claims to act for another actor. A feeder validates the concrete authority before delivery when the requested action is not directly eligible through a source channel. Mandate-backed authority uses Mandate/Mandate Authority.

message.description: Message or event recorded by the entry.

content.name: Trigger Event
content.description:
Workflow step that requests emission of a Blue event from the current invocation. Trigger Event constructs an event
payload and returns it as a processor effect. It does not directly deliver to external parties or arbitrary channels;
the Blue Contracts processor records, validates, charges, enqueues, bridges, routes, and exposes the emitted event
according to its event/FIFO/outbox rules.

Trigger Event is useful for notifying participants, asking another scope to act, producing domain events, or creating
follow-up Operation Requests. The event payload must be a valid Blue node. Construction work, such as BEX execution,
is charged by the compute/runtime layer; successful processor emission and routing are charged by Blue Contracts gas.

event.description:
Event payload to emit. It may be any valid Blue node accepted by the host processor. Undefined or invalid event
construction must fail before successful emission gas is charged.

content.name: Update Document
content.description:
Workflow step that requests selected-document mutation through the Blue Contracts patch pipeline. Update Document is
the controlled gateway for state changes in a sequential workflow. It takes a changeset produced by authoring, BEX,
prior steps, or host bindings, validates it, previews it when needed, and submits it to the processor as ordered patch
effects.

Every patch is processed under Blue Contracts rules: runtime pointer validation, scope boundary checks, reserved-key
protection, runtime insertion normalization, gas charging, post-patch type-soundness validation, dynamic type
generalization when a valid more-general type is required, Type Generalization Policy enforcement, and Document
Update cascade delivery. A patch that would leave the selected document inconsistent with its declared type must be
repaired by permitted generalization or rejected; the processor must not commit a document that lies about its type.

In sequential workflows, an implementation may maintain a frozen WorkingDocument. Applying an Update Document step to
that working state gives later steps read-your-writes behavior before the final effect buffer is committed. The
preview must use the same immutable patch planner and conformance/generalization logic as the final processor commit,
otherwise workflows could observe a state that the processor could not legally produce.

changeset.description:
Ordered list of patch entries to apply through the Blue Contracts processor. Each entry must be valid under the
processor patch rules. The order is significant: each patch is applied, type-checked/generalized, and cascaded before
the next patch is considered.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/AdjustableDate
content.description: A class for defining a date that shall be subject to adjustment if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business day in the specified business centers, together with the convention for adjusting the date.

adjustedDate.description: The date once the adjustment has been performed. (Note that this date may change if the business center holidays change).

dateAdjustments.description: The business day convention and financial business centers used for adjusting the date if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business date in the specified business centers.

dateAdjustmentsReference.description: A pointer style reference to date adjustments defined elsewhere in the document.

unadjustedDate.description: A date subject to adjustment. While in FpML this date is required, this cardinality constraint has been relaxed as part of the CDM in order to support the FRA representation, which effective and termination dates are specified in FpML as adjusted dates.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/AdjustableDates
content.description: A class for defining a series of dates that shall be subject to adjustment if they would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business day in the specified business centers, together with the convention for adjusting the dates.

adjustedDate.description: The date(s) once the adjustment has been performed. (Note that this date may change if the business center holidays change).

dateAdjustments.description: The business day convention and financial business centers used for adjusting the date if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business date in the specified business centers.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/AdjustableOrAdjustedDate
content.description: A class for defining a date that shall be subject to adjustment if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business day in the specified business centers, together with the convention for adjusting the date.

adjustedDate.description: The date once the adjustment has been performed. (Note that this date may change if the business center holidays change).

dateAdjustments.description: The business day convention and financial business centers used for adjusting the date if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business date in the specified business centers.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/AdjustableOrAdjustedOrRelativeDate
content.description: This Rosetta class specifies the date as either an unadjusted, adjusted or relative date. It supplements the features of the AdjustableOrAdjustedDate to support the credit default swap option premium, which uses the relative date construct.

adjustedDate.description: The date once the adjustment has been performed. (Note that this date may change if the business center holidays change).

dateAdjustments.description: The business day convention and financial business centers used for adjusting the date if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business date in the specified business centers.

relativeDate.description: A date specified as some offset to another date (the anchor date).

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/AdjustableOrRelativeDate
content.description: A class giving the choice between defining a date as an explicit date together with applicable adjustments or as relative to some other (anchor) date.

adjustableDate.description: A date that shall be subject to adjustment if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business day in the specified business centers, together with the convention for adjusting the date.

relativeDate.description: A date specified as some offset to another date (the anchor date).

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/AdjustableOrRelativeDates
content.description: A class giving the choice between defining a series of dates as an explicit list of dates together with applicable adjustments or as relative to some other series of (anchor) dates.

adjustableDates.description: A series of dates that shall be subject to adjustment if they would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business day in the specified business centers, together with the convention for adjusting the date.

relativeDates.description: A series of dates specified as some offset to another series of dates (the anchor dates).

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/AdjustableRelativeOrPeriodicDates
content.description: A class giving the choice between defining a series of dates as an explicit list of dates together with applicable adjustments or as relative to some other series of (anchor) dates, or as a calculation period schedule.

adjustableDates.description: A series of dates that shall be subject to adjustment if they would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business day in the specified business centers, together with the convention for adjusting the date.

relativeDates.description: A series of dates specified as some offset to another series of dates (the anchor dates).

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/AdjustedRelativeDateOffset
content.description: A type defining a date (referred to as the derived date) as a relative offset from another date (referred to as the anchor date) plus optional date adjustments.

adjustedDate.description: The date once the adjustment has been performed. (Note that this date may change if the business center holidays change).

businessCentersReference.description: A pointer style reference to a set of financial business centers defined elsewhere in the document. This set of business centers is used to determine whether a particular day is a business day or not.

businessDayConvention.description: The convention for adjusting a date if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business day, as specified by an ISDA convention (e.g. Following, Precedent).

dateRelativeTo.description: Specifies the anchor as an href attribute. The href attribute value is a pointer style reference to the element or component elsewhere in the document where the anchor date is defined.

dayType.description: In the case of an offset specified as a number of days, this element defines whether consideration is given as to whether a day is a good business day or not. If a day type of business days is specified then non-business days are ignored when calculating the offset. The financial business centers to use for determination of business days are implied by the context in which this element is used. This element must only be included when the offset is specified as a number of days. If the offset is zero days then the dayType element should not be included.

period.description: A time period, e.g. a day, week, month or year of the stream. If the periodMultiplier value is 0 (zero) then period must contain the value D (day).

periodMultiplier.description: A time period multiplier, e.g. 1, 2 or 3 etc. A negative value can be used when specifying an offset relative to another date, e.g. -2 days.

relativeDateAdjustments.description: The business day convention and financial business centers used for adjusting the relative date if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business date in the specified business centers.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/AveragingSchedule
content.description: Class to representing a method for generating a series of dates.

averagingPeriodFrequency.description: The frequency at which averaging period occurs with the regular part of the valuation schedule and their roll date convention.

endDate.description: Date on which this period ends.

startDate.description: Date on which this period begins.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/BusinessCenterEnum
content.description: The enumerated values to specify the business centers.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/BusinessCenterTime
content.description: A class for defining a time with respect to a business day calendar location. For example, 11:00:00 GBLO.

businessCenter.description: A code identifying a business day calendar location. A business day calendar location is drawn from the list identified by the business day calendar location enumeration.

hourMinuteTime.description: A time specified in hh:mm:ss format where the second component must be '00', e.g. 11am would be represented as 11:00:00.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/BusinessCenters
content.description: A class for specifying the business day calendar location used in determining whether a day is a business day or not, either by specifying this business center by reference to an enumerated list that is maintained by the FpML standard, or by reference to such specification when it exists elsewhere as part of the instance document. This class corresponds to the FpML BusinessCentersOrReference.model.

businessCenter.description: A code identifying one or several business day calendar location(s). The set of business day calendar locations are specified by the business day calendar location enumeration which is maintained by the FpML standard.

businessCentersReference.description: A reference to a financial business center location specified elsewhere in the instance document.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/BusinessDateRange
content.description: A class defining a range of contiguous business days by defining an unadjusted first date, an unadjusted last date and a business day convention and business centers for adjusting the first and last dates if they would otherwise fall on a non business day in the specified business centers. The days between the first and last date must also be good business days in the specified centers to be counted in the range.

businessCenters.description: The business center(s), specified either explicitly or by reference to those specified somewhere else in the instance document.

businessDayConvention.description: The convention for adjusting a date if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business day, as specified by an ISDA convention (e.g. Following, Precedent).

endDate.description: The last date of a date range.

startDate.description: The first date of a date range.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/BusinessDayAdjustments
content.description: A class defining the business day convention and financial business centers used for adjusting any relevant date if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business day in the specified business center.

businessCenters.description: The business center(s), specified either explicitly or by reference to those specified somewhere else in the instance document.

businessDayConvention.description: The convention for adjusting a date if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business day.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/BusinessDayConventionEnum
content.description: The enumerated values to specify the convention for adjusting any relevant date if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a valid business day.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/CalculationFrequency
content.description: Represents the parameters for describing how often something (such as collateral interest) is to be calculated.

businessCenter.description: Specifies the business center for adjustment of calculation period.

dateLocation.description: Specifies where is the time measured.

dayOfMonth.description: Specifies the day of the month if used.

dayOfWeek.description: Specifies the day of the week if used.

monthOfYear.description: Specifies the month of the year if used.

offsetDays.description: Specifies how many days from the trigger event should the payment occur.

period.description: Specifies the time period at which calculation is performed, e.g. 1 month.

weekOfMonth.description: Specifies the week of the month if used.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/CalculationPeriodFrequency
content.description: A class to specify the frequency at which calculation period end dates occur within the regular part of the calculation period schedule and their roll date convention.

balanceOfFirstPeriod.description: Indicates, when true, that that the first Calculation Period should run from the Effective Date to the end of the calendar period in which the Effective Date falls, e.g. Jan 15 - Jan 31 if the calculation periods are one month long and Effective Date is Jan 15. If false, the first Calculation Period should run from the Effective Date for one whole period, e.g. Jan 15 to Feb 14 if the calculation periods are one month long and Effective Date is Jan 15. Mostly used in Commmodity Swaps.

period.description: A time period, e.g. a day, week, month, year or term of the stream.

periodMultiplier.description: A time period multiplier, e.g. 1, 2, or 3. If the period value is T (Term) then period multiplier must contain the value 1.

rollConvention.description: The roll convention specifies the period term as part of a periodic schedule, i.e. the calculation period end date within the regular part of the calculation period. The value could be a rule, e.g. IMM Settlement Dates, which is the 3rd Wednesday of the month, or it could be a specific day of the month, such as the first day of the applicable month. It is used in conjunction with a frequency and the regular period start date of a calculation period.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/CompoundingTypeEnum
content.description: The enumerated values to specify how the compounding calculation is done

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/CustomisableOffset
content.description: A class to specify an offset either as a normalized [multiplier, period, dayType] or as a custom provision of type string.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/DateList
content.description: List of dates.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/DateRange
content.description: A class defining a contiguous series of calendar dates. The date range is defined as all the dates between and including the start and the end date. The start date must fall on or before the end date.

endDate.description: The last date of a date range.

startDate.description: The first date of a date range.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/DateTimeList
content.description: List of dateTimes.

dateTime.description: The CDM specifies that the zoned date time is to be expressed in accordance with ISO 8601, either as UTC as an offset to UTC.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/DayOfWeekEnum
content.description: The enumerated values to specify a day of the seven-day week.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/DayTypeEnum
content.description: Lists the enumerated values to specify the day type classification used in counting the number of days between two dates.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/Frequency
content.description: A class for defining a date frequency, e.g. one day, three months, through the combination of an integer value and a standardized period value that is specified as part of an enumeration.

period.description: A time period, e.g. a day, week, month, year or term of the stream.

periodMultiplier.description: A time period multiplier, e.g. 1, 2, or 3. If the period value is T (Term) then period multiplier must contain the value 1.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/Offset
content.description: A class defining an offset used in calculating a new date relative to a reference date, e.g. calendar days, business days, commodity Business days, etc.

dayType.description: In the case of an offset specified as a number of days, this element defines whether consideration is given as to whether a day is a good business day or not. If a day type of business days is specified then non-business days are ignored when calculating the offset. The financial business centers to use for determination of business days are implied by the context in which this element is used. This element must only be included when the offset is specified as a number of days. If the offset is zero days then the dayType element should not be included.

period.description: A time period, e.g. a day, week, month or year of the stream. If the periodMultiplier value is 0 (zero) then period must contain the value D (day).

periodMultiplier.description: A time period multiplier, e.g. 1, 2 or 3 etc. A negative value can be used when specifying an offset relative to another date, e.g. -2 days.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/Period
content.description: A class to define recurring periods or time offsets.

period.description: A time period, e.g. a day, week, month or year of the stream. If the periodMultiplier value is 0 (zero) then period must contain the value D (day).

periodMultiplier.description: A time period multiplier, e.g. 1, 2 or 3 etc. A negative value can be used when specifying an offset relative to another date, e.g. -2 days.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/PeriodBound
content.description: Indicator to specify if the period bound is defined as a period and whether the bound is inclusive.

inclusive.description: Specifies whether the period bound is inclusive, e.g. for a lower bound, false would indicate greater than, whereas true would indicate greater than or equal to.

period.description: Specifies the period is to be used as the bound, e.g. 5Y.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/PeriodEnum
content.description: The enumerated values to specify the period, e.g. day, week.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/PeriodExtendedEnum
content.description: The enumerated values to specify a time period containing the additional value of Term.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/PeriodRange
content.description: Indicates The period range defined as either a lower and upper period bound, or both.

lowerBound.description: Specifies the lower bound of a period range, e.g. greater than or equal to 5Y.

upperBound.description: Specifies the upper bound of a period range, e.g. less than to 10Y.

content.name: cdm/base/datetime/PeriodTimeEnum
