delivery.description: Contains the information relative to the delivery of the asset.

deliveryTerm.description: Also called contract month or delivery month. However, it's not always a month. It is usually expressed using a code, e.g. Z23 would be the Dec 2023 contract, (Z = December). For crude oil, the corresponding contract might be called CLZ23.

payerReceiver.description: Canonical representation of the payer and receiver parties applicable to each payout leg.

priceQuantity.description: Each payout leg must implement the quantity concept as a 'resolvable' type, which allows for different payout legs to be linked to each other (e.g. in the case of cross-curreny products).

principalPayment.description: The specification of the principal exchange. Optional as only applicable in the case of cross-currency or zero-coupon swaps with a final payment.

schedule.description: Allows the full representation of a payout by defining a set of schedule periods. It supports standard schedule customization by expressing all the dates, quantities, and pricing data in a non-parametric way.

settlementTerms.description: Each payout leg must specifies its settlement terms, including the delivery type (i.e. cash vs physical, and their respective terms), the transfer type (DvP etc.) and settlement date, if any.

underlier.description: The underlying financial product that will be physically or cash settled, which can be of any type, eg an asset such as cash or a security, or the cash settlement of an index rate.

content.name: cdm/product/template/StrategyFeature
content.description: A class for defining option strategy features.

calendarSpread.description: Definition of the later expiration date in a calendar spread.

strikeSpread.description: Definition of the upper strike in a strike spread.

content.name: cdm/product/template/Strike
content.description: A class describing a single cap or floor rate.

strikeRate.description: The rate for a cap or floor.

content.name: cdm/product/template/StrikeSchedule
content.description: A class describing a schedule of cap or floor rates.

price.description: The initial rate. An initial rate of 5% would be represented as 0.05.

content.name: cdm/product/template/StrikeSpread
content.description: A class for defining a strike spread feature.

upperStrike.description: Upper strike in a strike spread.

upperStrikeNumberOfOptions.description: Number of options at the upper strike price in a strike spread.

content.name: cdm/product/template/TerminationProvision
content.description: A class for defining option provisions.

cancelableProvision.description: A provision that allows the specification of an embedded option within a swap giving the buyer of the option the right to terminate the swap, in whole or in part, on the early termination date.

earlyTerminationProvision.description: Parameters specifying provisions relating to the optional and mandatory early termination of a swap transaction.

evergreenProvision.description: A data defining: the right of a party to exercise an Evergreen option

extendibleProvision.description: A provision that allows the specification of an embedded option with a swap giving the buyer of the option the right to extend the swap, in whole or in part, to the extended termination date.

content.name: cdm/product/template/TradableProduct
content.description: Definition of a product as ready to be traded, i.e. included in an execution or contract, by associating a specific price and quantity to this product plus an (optional) mechanism for any potential future quantity adjustment.

adjustment.description: Specifies the conditions that govern the adjustment to the quantity of a product being traded: e.g. execution, portfolio rebalancing etc. It is typically used in the context of Equity Swaps.

ancillaryParty.description: Specifies the parties with ancillary roles in the transaction. The product is agnostic to the actual parties involved in the transaction, with the party references abstracted away from the product definition and replaced by the AncillaryRoleEnum. The AncillaryRoleEnum can then be positioned in the product and this AncillaryParty type, which is positioned outside of the product definition, allows the AncillaryRoleEnum to be associated with an actual party reference.

counterparty.description: Specifies the parties which are the two counterparties to the transaction.  The product is agnostic to the actual parties to the transaction, with the party references abstracted away from the product definition and replaced by the counterparty enum (e.g. CounterpartyEnum values Party1 or Party2). The counterparty enum can then be positioned in the product (e.g. to specify which counterparty is the payer, receiver etc) and this counterparties attribute, which is positioned outside of the product definition, allows the counterparty enum to be associated with an actual party reference.

product.description: The underlying product to be included in a contract or execution.

tradeLot.description: Specifies the price, quantity and effective date of each trade lot, when the same product may be traded multiple times in different lots with the same counterparty. In a trade increase, a new trade lot is added to the list, with the corresponding effective date. In a trade decrease, the existing trade lot(s) are decreased of the corresponding quantity (and an unwind fee may have to be settled). The multiple cardinality and the ability to increase existing trades is used for Equity Swaps in particular.

content.name: cdm/product/template/TradeLot
content.description: Specifies the price and quantity of a trade lot, where the same product could be traded multiple times with the same counterparty but in different lots (at a different date, in a different quantity and at a different price). One trade lot combined with a product definition specifies the entire economics of a trade. The lifecycle mechanics of each such trade lot (e.g. cashflow payments) is independent of the other lots.

lotIdentifier.description: Specifies one or more identifiers for the lot, if any.

priceQuantity.description: Specifies the settlement characteristics of a trade lot: price, quantity, observable (optionally) and the settlement terms. This attribute has a multiple cardinality to allow to specify the price, quantity and observable of different legs in a single, composite product (e.g. a Swap).

content.name: cdm/product/template/TransferableProduct
content.description: A TransferableProduct is a type of financial product which can be held or transferred, represented as an Asset with the addition of specific EconomicTerms.

Cash.description: An Asset that consists solely of a monetary holding in a currency.

Commodity.description: An Asset comprised of raw or refined materials or agricultural products, eg gold, oil or wheat.

DigitalAsset.description: An Asset that exists only in digital form, eg Bitcoin or Ethereum; excludes the digital representation of other Assets.

economicTerms.description: The price forming features, including payouts and provisions.

Instrument.description: An asset that is issued by one party to one or more others; Instrument is also a choice data type.

content.name: cdm/product/template/Underlier
content.description: The underlying financial product that will be physically or cash settled, which can be of any type, eg an asset such as cash or a security, a product, or the cash settlement of an index rate.  Conditions are usually applied when used in a data type, such as a payout, to ensure this aligns with the use case.

Observable.description: Specifies the object to be observed for a price, it could be an asset or a reference.

Product.description: Enables either a TransferableProduct or a NonTransferableProduct to be used in an underlier.

content.name: Document Responder Mandate
content.description: Mandate authorizing the actor bound to authorizedActorChannel to respond to covered requests emitted by sessions of authorizedInitialDocument. The concrete request shape and additional conditions are defined through the inherited validation fields.

authorizedInitialDocument.description: Initial document whose sessions may emit covered requests.

content.name: Mandate
content.description:
Base executable document type for guaranteed authority delegation.

The actor bound to authorityHolderChannel controls the authority or resource
being delegated. The actor bound to authorizedActorChannel receives the
delegated authority. The actor bound to mandateGuarantorChannel confirms that
the declared authority relationship is legitimate and may terminate the
mandate.

Authority confirmation and activation are separate lifecycle facts.
Confirmation records that the guarantor accepted the authority declaration.
Activation records the timestamp from which the authorized actor may use the
delegated authority.

By default, successful authority confirmation emits Mandate/Mandate
Activated for the inherited activation workflow to apply. A mandate may set
activateOnAuthorityConfirmation to false and define an additional operation
that emits Mandate/Mandate Activated when a later condition is satisfied.

The base type defines and implements initialization, authority confirmation,
activation, termination, lifecycle event emission, lifecycle transition
guards, and graceful mandate-document termination. Subtypes inherit these
lifecycle implementations unchanged. They may add specialized fields,
validation, participants, embedded documents, and operations that emit the
standard activation or termination Messages.

mandateGuarantorChannel.description:
Required participant channel whose actor is the mandate guarantor.

The guarantor confirms that the declared authority relationship is
legitimate and may invoke the standard termination operation.

authorityHolderChannel.description:
Required participant channel whose actor controls the authority or
resource delegated by this mandate. The authority holder may invoke the
standard termination operation.

authorizedActorChannel.description:
Required participant channel whose actor receives the delegated
authority. Concrete mandate subtypes define the delegated resource,
action, target, or request semantics.

mandateTerminationChannel.description:
Composite channel through which either the guarantor or authority holder
may invoke terminateMandate. When one entry is eligible through both
members, the composite produces one logical delivery.

mandateLifecycleChannel.description:
Processor-managed lifecycle channel used by the inherited initialization
workflow.

mandateActivatedChannel.description:
Internal triggered-event channel routing Mandate/Mandate Activated
Messages emitted by confirmation or specialized mandate operations.
External Timeline Entries do not enter this channel directly.

mandateTerminatedChannel.description:
Internal triggered-event channel routing Mandate/Mandate Terminated
Messages emitted by the standard termination operation or specialized
mandate operations.

mandateLifecycleDefinition.description:
Canonical reusable BEX implementation of mandate lifecycle transitions.
It contains deterministic functions used by initializeMandate,
confirmMandateAuthority, applyMandateActivation, and
applyMandateTermination. Subtypes do not replace these functions.

inResponseTo.description: Exact Message answered by this lifecycle Message.

request.description: Operation request payload containing the required reason.

then.value: validation.function.functions must declare the entry named by validation.function.entry.

initializeMandate.description:
Inherited initialization implementation.

Normal Blue type resolution and bootstrap validate required role-channel
bindings and lifecycle configuration. When validation.function.entry is
present, this workflow verifies that validation.function.functions
declares the selected local function.

On success it materializes activateOnAuthorityConfirmation as true when
absent and sets status to Coordination/Status Pending.

On failure it sets status to Coordination/Status Failed, stores the
first deterministic failure in initializationError.

Initialization does not write, clear, or normalize lifecycle timestamps.

Concrete workflow steps and BEX implementation are defined in this base
type.

confirmMandateAuthority.description:
Inherited operation through which the guarantor confirms that the
declared authority relationship is legitimate.

On Coordination/Status Pending it changes status to
Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed, records authorityConfirmedAt
from the root causal Timeline Entry, emits Mandate/Mandate Authority
Confirmed, and, when activateOnAuthorityConfirmation is not false, emits
Mandate/Mandate Activated for the inherited activation workflow.

On Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed, Mandate/Status Active,
Mandate/Status Terminated, or Coordination/Status Failed it performs no
lifecycle mutation and does not replace authorityConfirmedAt.

A guarantor may choose to use Operation Request.document and
requireExactDocumentVersion to pin the reviewed mandate state. This base
operation does not require or enforce that choice.

Concrete workflow steps and BEX implementation are defined in this base
type.

applyMandateActivation.description:
Sole authoritative mandate-activation implementation.

It accepts Mandate/Mandate Activated emitted by an operation. On
Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed it changes status to Mandate/Status
Active and records activatedAt from the root causal Timeline Entry. The
Message itself does not supply the timestamp and is not emitted again.

On Coordination/Status Pending, Mandate/Status Active,
Mandate/Status Terminated, or Coordination/Status Failed it performs no
lifecycle mutation and does not replace activatedAt.

A Message without a root causal Timeline Entry cannot establish an
activation timestamp and must not activate the mandate.

Concrete workflow steps and BEX implementation are defined in this base
type.

terminateMandate.description:
Standard termination operation available to the guarantor and authority
holder.

Unless the mandate is already Mandate/Status Terminated, it emits
Mandate/Mandate Terminated with the required request reason and
correlation to the invoking Message. This includes a failed mandate,
allowing the guarantor or authority holder to stop its processing. The
operation does not write lifecycle state directly;
applyMandateTermination remains the sole authoritative termination
implementation.

On Mandate/Status Terminated it emits no lifecycle Message. Specialized
mandate types may add other operations that emit Mandate/Mandate
Terminated.

Concrete workflow steps are defined in this base type.

reason.description: Required human-readable or machine-generated termination reason.

applyMandateTermination.description:
Sole authoritative mandate-termination implementation.

It accepts Mandate/Mandate Terminated emitted by an operation. On
Coordination/Status Pending, Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed, or
Mandate/Status Active it changes status to Mandate/Status Terminated and
records terminatedAt from the root causal Timeline Entry. The Message
itself carries the required reason and correlation, does not supply the
timestamp, and is not emitted again. Its reason is propagated unchanged
to the graceful processor termination request.

The Compute result requests graceful termination after its state changes
and emitted events have been buffered. Coordination validates the complete
result before applying effects, then applies changes, emits events, and
requests graceful termination in that order.

On Mandate/Status Terminated or Coordination/Status Failed it performs no
lifecycle mutation and does not replace terminatedAt. Receipt of the
termination Message still requests graceful processing termination, so a
failed mandate can be stopped without replacing its failure state.

Concrete workflow steps and BEX implementation are defined in this base
type. No dedicated termination workflow-step type is required.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the mandate.

Initialization sets exactly one initial status:

- Coordination/Status Pending when deterministic initialization succeeds.
- Coordination/Status Failed when deterministic initialization fails.

Supported transitions are:

- Coordination/Status Pending -> Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed
- Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed -> Mandate/Status Active
- Coordination/Status Pending -> Mandate/Status Terminated
- Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed -> Mandate/Status Terminated
- Mandate/Status Active -> Mandate/Status Terminated

Coordination/Status Failed and Mandate/Status Terminated are terminal.
Lifecycle workflows do not replace timestamps or statuses after the
corresponding transition succeeds.

initializationError.description:
First deterministic initialization error when status is
Coordination/Status Failed.

Initialization writes this field only when initialization fails and stops
at the first material error rather than accumulating an error list. A
successful initialization does not write, clear, or normalize a value
already present in an authored document.

activateOnAuthorityConfirmation.description:
Controls whether successful authority confirmation also emits the mandate
activation Message.

When true, successful confirmation emits Mandate/Mandate Activated, which
is handled by the inherited activation workflow.

When false, successful confirmation leaves the mandate in
Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed. A specialized operation must later emit
Mandate/Mandate Activated.

When absent before initialization, the initialization workflow materializes
true. The field is not a fixed inherited value, so a concrete mandate may
explicitly set it to false.

authorityConfirmedAt.description:
Microsecond timestamp of the root causal Coordination/Timeline Entry that
successfully changed the mandate from Coordination/Status Pending to
Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed.

The value is derived by the inherited authority-confirmation workflow. It
is never supplied by the operation request. After authority confirmation
succeeds, inherited lifecycle workflows do not replace it.

activatedAt.description:
Microsecond timestamp from which the mandate entered Mandate/Status Active.

The value is derived by the inherited activation workflow from the root
causal Coordination/Timeline Entry that led to the accepted
Mandate/Mandate Activated Message. It is not supplied by that Message.
After activation succeeds, inherited lifecycle workflows do not replace
it.

terminatedAt.description:
Microsecond timestamp from which the mandate entered Mandate/Status Terminated.

The value is derived by the inherited termination workflow from the root
causal Coordination/Timeline Entry that led to the accepted
Mandate/Mandate Terminated Message. It is not supplied by that Message.
After termination succeeds, inherited lifecycle workflows do not replace
it.

validation.description:
Optional request-validation convention inherited by mandate subtypes.

A concrete mandate type defines which request or event is matched by
validation.request and which runtime component performs the validation.
Mandate/Operation Mandate matches the Operation Request payload.
Document-responder and MyOS mandate types may validate an entire request
Message.

content.name: Mandate Activated
content.description:
Lifecycle Message emitted by authority confirmation or another authorized
mandate operation.

The inherited activation workflow accepts this Message while the mandate is
in Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed, changes the status to
Mandate/Status Active, and derives activatedAt from the root causal Timeline
Entry. This Message does not supply the effective timestamp and is not
re-emitted by the accepting workflow. The inherited inResponseTo field may
identify the Message that caused activation.

content.name: Mandate Authority
content.description: Authority evidence backed by an initial Mandate/Mandate document. On a Timeline Entry, the containing actor claims to act on behalf of actor under that mandate. The initialMandateDocument value may be materialized inline or represented as an equivalent pure { blueId: ... } reference.

actor.description: Actor on whose behalf the containing actor claims to act.

initialMandateDocument.description: Initial mandate document authorizing the represented authority relationship. A feeder or provider resolves the exact processed mandate state required for the relevant action timestamp.

content.name: Mandate Authority Confirmed
content.description:
Authoritative Message emitted when the inherited mandate workflow
successfully confirms the declared authority relationship.

Confirmation does not necessarily activate the mandate. When immediate
activation is enabled, the same operation also emits Mandate Activated for
the inherited activation workflow to apply.

timestampUs.description: Authority-confirmation timestamp derived from the root causal Timeline Entry.

content.name: Mandate Terminated
content.description:
Lifecycle Message emitted by the standard termination operation or another
authorized mandate operation.

The inherited termination workflow applies the terminal lifecycle transition
when the current status permits it, derives terminatedAt from the root causal
Timeline Entry, and requests graceful processing termination. A failed
mandate may therefore stop processing without replacing its failure state.
This Message does not supply the effective timestamp and is not re-emitted by
the accepting workflow. The inherited inResponseTo field may identify the
Message that invoked termination.

reason.description:
Required human-readable or machine-generated termination reason. The
inherited termination workflow propagates this value unchanged to the
graceful processor termination request.

content.name: Mandate Validation
content.description:
Optional static and deterministic request-validation configuration used by
Mandate documents. The containing concrete mandate type defines the input
examined by this configuration and the runtime component that invokes it.

Validation passes only when both configured checks pass: request is absent or
matches the candidate input, and function is absent or evaluates to Boolean
true for that same input.

request.description:
Optional static Blue pattern matched against the input defined by the
concrete mandate type. When absent, static request-shape matching imposes
no additional restriction.

The same candidate input is passed to function as the immutable BEX binding
named request.

function.description:
Optional deterministic BEX validation program represented as a Blue node.
This field intentionally has no repository-local nominal BEX type: program
syntax and compilation are defined by the BEX specification and runtime.

By convention, the host passes the candidate input being validated as the
immutable BEX binding named request. Concrete mandate types define the
semantic meaning of that input.

A concrete mandate document may define function.entry to select a local
function. When present, function.functions must declare a callable function
with exactly that name. The feeder or provider invokes the selected entry
without arguments; the candidate input remains available through the
request binding.

When function is absent, function validation passes. When present, only the
Boolean result true passes. False, null, undefined, a non-Boolean result, or
deterministic compilation or execution failure rejects the candidate.

content.name: Operation Mandate
content.description:
Mandate authorizing the actor bound to authorizedActorChannel to invoke one
named operation through one exact effective channel, on behalf of the actor
bound to authorityHolderChannel.

It may be used on any target where the authority-holder actor participates in
the declared effective channel and all inherited lifecycle, actor, channel,
operation, document-version, and optional validation checks pass.

The inherited validation field examines the nested Operation Request.request
payload through its immutable request binding. It does not examine the target
document or Operation Request envelope.

Optional target.documentValidation examines only the frozen resolved target
root immediately before the candidate Timeline Entry. Its absence imposes no
target-document identity, type, or content restriction.

channel.description: Exact effective target channel authorized by this mandate.

operation.description: Single target operation authorized by this mandate.

documentValidation.description:
Optional deterministic target-document validation. Absence imposes no
document identity, type, or content restriction. When present, at least
one matcher is required and both configured matchers must pass.

document.description:
Optional structural Blue pattern matched candidate-first against the
frozen resolved target root immediately before the candidate entry.
Extra fields in the candidate are allowed; every omitted field is
unconstrained.

function.description:
Optional deterministic BEX validation program represented as a Blue
node. The host exposes $document as the exact resolved Mandate root and
targetDocument as the sole immutable candidate binding containing the
frozen resolved pre-entry target root.

It does not expose the operation request or other ambient bindings.
Request validation belongs to the inherited validation field.

Only Boolean true passes. False, null, undefined, a non-Boolean result,
compilation failure, execution failure, or resource-limit failure
rejects the candidate.

content.name: Status Active
content.description: Mandate lifecycle status indicating that the guarantor-confirmed authority is currently usable by the authorized actor, subject to the concrete mandate's target and request constraints. The mandate may transition from this status only to Mandate/Status Terminated.

content.name: Status Authority Confirmed
content.description: Mandate lifecycle status indicating that the mandate guarantor has confirmed the declared authority relationship, while the delegated authority is not yet active. The mandate may transition from this status to Mandate/Status Active or Mandate/Status Terminated.

content.name: Status Terminated
content.description: Terminal mandate lifecycle status indicating that the delegated authority has permanently ended. A mandate in this status cannot be confirmed, activated, or terminated again, and the mandate processing document is gracefully terminated after the status and authoritative termination Message are stored.

participantBinding.description: How to identify the new user.

content.name: MyOS Agent Operation Mandate
content.description:
Reusable Operation Mandate allowing one MyOS Agent Actor to invoke the
inherited operation for matching target documents on behalf of one MyOS
Principal Actor.

The optional ordered rules list contains owner-readable instructions for a
constrained MyOS intelligent evaluator. The inherited request and target
document validation may deterministically constrain the operation, while
rules may provide an additional or sole target-eligibility gate. The feeder
never interprets rule text or invokes a model.

rules.description:
Optional ordered immutable rules. An absent or empty list means that no
intelligent evaluation is required. Rule IDs must be non-blank and unique
within the exact mandate state; the MyOS host enforces those constraints.

content.name: MyOS Agent Operation Rule
content.description: Owner-readable instruction used by the constrained MyOS intelligent evaluator for one candidate action.

id.description: Stable unique rule identifier within this exact mandate state.

text.description: Owner-readable instruction evaluated for each candidate action.

content.name: MyOS Balance Account
content.description: A prepared or direct MyOS balance-account reference used in payment requests.

token.description: Opaque token representing a prepared recipient payment target.

content.name: MyOS Document Bootstrap Mandate
content.description: MyOS-hosted responder mandate allowing sessions of the inherited authorizedInitialDocument to request bootstrap work from MyOS Admin. The canonical subtype constrains the guarantor and authorized-actor roles to MyOS Admin. Allowed document, channel-binding, initial-message, and on-behalf-of constraints are expressed through inherited validation.

content.description: A reference to a specific, live document processing session on the MyOS platform.

documentId.description: The initial blueId of the logical document.

sessionId.description: The id of a specific, live processing session.

content.name: MyOS Operation Call Requested
content.description: Request asking MyOS Admin to prepare an Operation Request for a target document. This request is not authority. Before delegated execution, MyOS must select and verify one exact active MyOS Agent Operation Mandate, and the target Timeline Entry must carry the corresponding Mandate Authority.

document.description: Current target document state used as the basis for the call.

requireExactDocumentVersion.description: Whether the target Operation Request requires exact target-state equality.

content.name: MyOS Session Subscription Ended
content.description: Response indicating that a root or linked-document subscription stream has ended. No further updates for this sourceInitialDocument are delivered under the identified subscription unless a future reinitiation protocol creates a new active stream.

sourceInitialDocument.description: Initial document identifying the ended root or linked-document stream.

reason.description: End reason, such as Requested, MandateTerminated, SourceUnavailable, Unlinked, or ProviderStopped.

content.name: MyOS Session Subscription Filter
content.description: Selects emitted events and processed document snapshots delivered for one source document in a MyOS session subscription.

events.description: Optional emitted-event filter. When omitted, all emitted events are included. An empty list includes no emitted events. A non-empty list includes only events matching at least one listed type or pattern.

initial.description: Whether the subscription start Message includes the initial processed document snapshot. When omitted, false.

include.description: Snapshot delivery mode: None, All, or WhenEventsMatched. None includes no ongoing snapshots. All includes every delivered epoch snapshot. WhenEventsMatched includes a snapshot only when at least one event matched in that epoch. When omitted, None.

content.name: MyOS Session Subscription Mandate
content.description: MyOS-hosted responder mandate allowing sessions of the inherited authorizedInitialDocument to request a provider-mediated subscription to a source logical document. The authority holder must control the source document or the explicitly constrained source session. The canonical subtype constrains the guarantor and authorized-actor roles to MyOS Admin.

sourceInitialDocument.description: Initial document whose selected session may be observed.

sourceDocumentSessionId.description: Optional concrete source session. When absent, MyOS Admin chooses an eligible session of sourceInitialDocument.

allowedAnchors.description: Optional anchors from which linked-document subscriptions may be requested. More detailed filter restrictions may be expressed through inherited validation.

content.name: MyOS Session Subscription Requested
content.description: Request asking MyOS Admin to start a provider-mediated subscription to a logical source document. The request targets a document, not a specific session. MyOS Admin chooses an eligible session unless the matching mandate constrains one. The subscriber is inferred from the requesting document session.

filter.description: Optional filter for the root source document.

anchor.description: Link anchor whose linked documents should be observed.

filter.description: Optional filter for linked documents under this anchor. When absent, defaults include all events and no snapshots.

content.name: MyOS Session Subscription Started
content.description: First update of a MyOS session subscription. It marks the clear start boundary of the stream and may carry the initial source snapshot when requested by the filter, together with any matching events delivered at that boundary.

content.name: MyOS Session Subscription Update
content.description: Provider-mediated subscription update for one logical source document. The same subscriptionId is used for the root source and derived linked-document streams. sourceInitialDocument identifies the logical document represented by this update.

subscriptionId.description: Stable identifier of the subscription stream.

sourceInitialDocument.description: Initial document identifying the logical source of this update.

document.description: Optional processed source-document snapshot selected by the filter.

events.description: Matching emitted events for the delivered source epoch; may be empty.

content.name: Accept Change Operation
content.description:
Operation marker for accepting a previously stored proposed change. Acceptance means the document should apply the
changes contained in proposal state and remove the proposal record once the processor has committed the change.

This operation is part of the proposal/accept/reject workflow family. It separates review from mutation: Propose Change
captures a request, Accept Change applies it, and Reject Change discards it. The corresponding Accept Change Workflow
performs validation, policy checks, translation of sectionChanges, and final Update Document patching.

content.name: Accept Change Workflow
content.description: Applies a previously proposed change and removes its proposal state.

content.name: Change Operation
content.description:
Operation marker for applying a Change Request immediately rather than first storing it as a proposal. It is intended
for contexts where the caller is already authorized to request the change and the document policy allows direct
application.

The operation's `request` shape is Workflows/Change Request. The corresponding Change Workflow validates the request,
blocks forbidden `/contracts` modifications when Contracts Change Policy requires sectionChanges, rejects attempts to
mutate proposal state recursively, and then applies the changes through Update Document.

Use this operation when immediate mutation is acceptable. Use Propose Change Operation followed by Accept or Reject when
changes must be reviewed before becoming document state.

content.name: Change Request
content.description:
Payload type for direct and proposed document-change operations. A Change Request describes what the caller wants to
change, why it is being changed, and—when contract mutation is governed by section policy—how the change maps to
logical document sections.

`summary` is the human-readable explanation required when a proposal is stored for later acceptance. `changeset` is the
list of patch entries for ordinary selected-document fields. `sectionChanges` is the structured form for modifying the
document's `contracts` map through Document Section markers when Contracts Change Policy is enabled. This split exists
so participants can review contract changes by section instead of accepting arbitrary low-level `/contracts` patches.

A Change Request is data. It does not mutate by itself. Change Workflow, Propose Change Workflow, Accept Change
Workflow, and Reject Change Workflow interpret it and produce processor patches or invalid-proposal events.

summary.description: Human-readable summary of the requested change. Required when proposal is created.

changeset.description: RFC 6902 patch entries outside /contracts (blocked by policy if it touches /contracts).

sectionChanges.description: Section-based /contracts mutations (required when Contracts Change Policy is enabled).

content.description: Applies a requested changeset immediately to the document.

content.name: Contracts Change Policy
content.description:
Marker contract that controls how the document's `contracts` map may be changed by coordination workflows. When
`requireSectionChanges` is present and not false, workflows such as Change Workflow and Accept Change Workflow must
reject raw changeset entries that directly target `/contracts`; callers must instead use structured `sectionChanges`.

The purpose is reviewability and safety. Contract entries define runtime behavior, channels, handlers, policies,
sections, and operations. Arbitrary low-level patches to `/contracts` are hard for humans and agents to audit. By
requiring Document Section Changes, this marker forces contract edits to be grouped by section with explicit related
contracts and section metadata.

This marker is interpreted by the coordination change workflows, not by the Blue Language. A processor or workflow that
does not support this policy should treat it according to its must-understand and contract capability rules.

requireSectionChanges.description: Policy flag; when present and not false, /contracts changes must use sectionChanges. Set false to allow direct changeset edits.

content.name: Document Section
content.description:
Marker contract that identifies a logical section of a document and links that section to the fields and contracts
responsible for it. A section gives humans, agents, and change-management workflows a coherent unit of meaning such as
payment setup, shipping details, consent terms, participant configuration, or embedded-order handling.

`title` and `summary` describe the section in user-facing terms. `relatedFields` lists absolute document pointers for
state fields covered by the section. `relatedContracts` lists same-scope contract keys that implement, enforce, or
affect the section. Section-aware workflows use this information to group proposed contract changes, validate that
contract edits belong to the right section, and present changes for review.

Document Section is metadata with runtime relevance only for workflows that understand it. It is also identity-bearing
document content. Changing a section's title, summary, fields, or related contracts changes what the document says
about its own structure and review surface.

title.description: Short, human-readable title shown in UI summaries.

summary.description: Brief functional summary of the section's purpose and behavior.

relatedFields.description: Absolute JSON Pointer paths of fields covered by this section.

relatedContracts.description: Contract keys in the same scope that implement or affect the section.

content.name: Document Section Change Entry
content.description:
One entry in a structured Document Section Changes request. It supplies the section key to add or modify, the Document
Section marker to store at that key, and the contracts that belong to the section. Change-management workflows convert
this structured entry into deterministic `/contracts` patches.

The `sectionKey` is the key under `/contracts` for the Document Section marker. The `section` node should be a
Workflows/Document Section whose `relatedContracts` corresponds to the keys in `contracts`, unless the workflow
fills or normalizes that relationship. The `contracts` map contains the actual contract nodes to add or replace for
the section.

This representation is intentionally higher-level than raw JSON patch. It lets policies require that behavioral changes
be reviewed as sections rather than as arbitrary pointer edits.

contracts.description: Map of contractKey -> contract node to add or replace for this section.

sectionKey.description: Contracts key under /contracts for the Document Section marker.

section.description: Document Section contract node; must include type Workflows/Document Section and relatedContracts should list keys in contracts.

content.name: Document Section Changes
content.description:
Structured collection of section-based contract mutations. It divides `/contracts` changes into `add`, `modify`, and
`remove` lists so a workflow can validate and apply them coherently under Contracts Change Policy.

`add` creates new Document Section markers and their related contracts. `modify` replaces an existing section's marker
and related contracts with a full new section definition. `remove` deletes a section key and the contracts listed as
related to that section. The exact patch sequence is produced by the supporting workflow, but the semantic intent is
section-level contract evolution rather than low-level pointer editing.

This type is useful for human review, AI-agent proposal validation, and audit trails because it preserves why a set of
contract changes belong together.

add.description: New sections to create with their Document Section and contracts.

modify.description: Existing sections to update with a full contracts map.

remove.description: Section keys to remove (also removes the section's related contracts).

content.name: Propose Change Operation
content.description:
Operation marker for proposing a Change Request without applying it immediately. The operation records a proposed
change under proposal state so another participant or policy-controlled workflow can later accept or reject it.

Propose Change is used when a document requires review, approval, negotiation, or human consent before applying a
mutation. The request shape is Workflows/Change Request, including a summary and optional structured sectionChanges.
The operation itself only declares the action; the paired Propose Change Workflow implements storage and validation.

content.name: Propose Change Workflow
content.description: Stores a proposed change under /proposedChange{postfix}.

request.description: Expected request payload for this workflow.

postfix.description: Optional postfix used while building proposed change state key.

content.name: Proposed Change Invalid
content.description:
Event emitted when a proposed, accepted, rejected, or direct change request cannot be processed under the document's
change-management rules. The event communicates a deterministic reason such as missing summary, missing proposal,
duplicate proposal, forbidden `/contracts` mutation, malformed sectionChanges, or another validation failure.

This event is intended to be observable by users, agents, and audit tools. It signals that the requested change did not
become document state. The `reason` field should be human-readable and stable enough for diagnostics, but it is not a
substitute for the processor's formal error category when the processor itself terminates fatally.

content.name: Reject Change Operation
content.description:
Operation marker for rejecting a previously proposed change. Rejection removes proposal state without applying the
requested changes. It is used when a reviewer, participant, or policy decides that the proposed mutation should not
become part of the document.

Reject Change complements Propose Change and Accept Change. The operation itself declares the action; the paired Reject
Change Workflow checks that proposal state exists and removes it through an Update Document step. If no proposal exists
at the expected path, the workflow emits Proposed Change Invalid.

content.name: Reject Change Workflow
content.description: Discards a previously proposed change by removing its proposal state.

postfix.description: Optional postfix used while building proposed change state key.
